page: Microsoft Azure D64ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V, running on an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 64 dedicated vCPUs spanning 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 256.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per vCPU). Fast local scratch capacity is provided via 3780 GB of attached NVMe SSD storage, and the hardware platform includes advanced vector and cryptographic instructions such as AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16), AES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate top-tier compute and data processing capabilities. Single-core stress-ng reached 3766.97, placing it in the top 10%, while multi-core stress-ng scored 118560.52 within the top 25%. The PassMark CPU suite scored 94549.31 and the extended instructions test reached 105850.51, both in the top 10%. Memory subsystem bandwidth registers 205.9 GB/sec read and 132.81 GB/sec write on uncached 256MB blocks. Compression operations are similarly robust, showing single-threaded gzip throughput of 41.18 GB/sec and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression at 424.87 GB/sec.

The server demonstrates high application throughput across multiple operational workloads, registering top 10% PassMark database performance at 36882.3 operations, 102.79 million Redis SET operations per second, and 72.71 GB/sec in static web serving. Without dedicated GPU acceleration, CPU-based large language model inference shows strong efficiency on smaller topologies (4989.67 prompt tokens/sec and 392.23 text generation tokens/sec on 135M models; 44.15 generation tokens/sec on 7B models), though it scales down to average tier performance on 70B models (4.7 tokens/sec generation).

Given its 64 dedicated cores, 256 GB of memory, and 3780 GB NVMe local disk, Microsoft Azure D64ads_v7 offers solid resource density for high-concurrency enterprise services, relational or NoSQL database workloads requiring quick scratch storage, real-time caching layers, and intermediate-scale CPU inference pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D64ads_v7 is a general-purpose instance featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs derived from a 32-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at up to 4.5 GHz, 256.0 GB of memory, and 3780 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system supports modern instruction extensions including AVX-512 (VNNI, BF16) and cryptographic acceleration. In benchmark assessments, it achieves top-tier results in single-core stress-ng (3766.97), PassMark CPU (94549.31), and PassMark database operations (36882.3), coupled with 102.79 million Redis SET operations per second and 205.9 GB/sec uncached read memory bandwidth. Lacking dedicated GPU hardware, the VM maintains strong execution speeds for small-to-medium CPU inference tasks alongside core enterprise applications. Its balance of compute power, high-bandwidth memory, and large local NVMe storage suits large database servers, memory-intensive caches, batch data processing, and enterprise web serving tiers.
